The '''Academy for the Mathematical Sciences''' is a UK [[national academy]].  Founded in 2023, the Academy aims to provide an authoritative and unified voice for mathematics in public life and policy, promoting the discipline’s contributions to national and global challenges in areas such as artificial intelligence, climate science, education, national security and economic resilience.  The first president is Dame [[Alison Etheridge]], a professor at the Department of Statistics, [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://chalkdustmagazine.com/interviews/in-conversation-with-alison-etheridge/|title=In conversation with Alison Etheridge|magazine=Chalkdust|year=2025|author=Elinor Flavell|ISSN=2059-3805|issue=21|pages=3-6}}</ref>

==Origins==
A national academy was formally proposed in a report by [[Philip Bond (mathematician)|Philip Bond]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/calls-for-evidence/national-academy-for-the-mathematical-sciences-proposed-focus-and-objectives/national-academy-for-mathematical-sciences|title=National academy for the mathematical sciences: proposed focus and objectives|year=2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite report|author=[[Philip Bond (mathematician)|Philip Bond]]|url=https://www.ukri.org/publications/the-era-of-mathematics/|title=The Era of Mathematics|publisher=[[UKRI]]|year=2018}}</ref> and a detailed prospectus was produced by the [[Council for the Mathematical Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/policy/council-mathematical-sciences|title=Council for the Mathematical Sciences|publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]]}}</ref> Growing applications of mathematical modelling and data science in stimulating demand for mathematical scientists were supported by a longer running concern that maths was neglected in public policy.<ref>{{cite report|title=Tackling the Mathematics Problem|url=https://studylib.net/doc/10501546/tackling-the-mathematics-problem |publisher=University of Birmingham|author=London Mathematical Society|year=1995}}</ref> The UK government agreed in principle to support a new academy and launched a consultation on the requirements,<ref>{{cite new|url=https://www.fenews.co.uk/skills/experts-and-sector-leaders-invited-to-shape-new-uk-national-maths-academy/|date=2024-01-12|title=Experts and sector leaders invited to shape new UK National Maths Academy|publisher=FE News}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|publisher=Times Higher Education|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/uk-plans-national-academy-mathematics|title=UK plans national academy for mathematics|date=2024-01-15|author=Patrick Jack}}</ref> followed by inviting bids to host the new body.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-offer-6m-to-organisations-to-help-creation-of-a-new-uk-national-academy-dedicated-to-maths|title=UK offer £6 million to organisations to help creation of a new UK National Academy dedicated to maths|year=2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fenews.co.uk/fe-voices/uk-offer-6m-to-organisations-to-help-creation-of-a-new-national-academy-for-mathematical-sciences/|date=2024-05-07|author=Gavin O'Meara|publisher=FE News|title=UK offer £6m to organisations to help creation of a new National Academy for Mathematical Sciences}}</ref>

Although £6M over three years had been committed in the [[November_2023_United_Kingdom_autumn_statement|2023 Autumn Statement]], after the [[2024_United_Kingdom_general_election|2024 General Election]], the new Labour administration withdrew financial support. This was acrimonious as no specific allocation had been made but funding was hypothecated on the [[treasury reserve]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/public-spending-what-is-the-treasury-reserve/|publisher=[[House of Commons Library]]|date=2024-09-25|title=Public spending: What is the Treasury Reserve?|author=Philip Brian}}</ref> and neither government nor opposition took responsibility for letting down the mathematics community.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.researchprofessionalnews.com/rr-news-uk-politics-2024-9-government-scraps-planned-national-academy-for-mathematics/|publisher=Research Professional News|author=Frances Jones|title=Government scraps planned national academy for mathematics|date=2024-09-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|publisher=[[Times Higher Education]]|date=2024-09-26|title=Labour scraps UK’s planned national academy for mathematics|author=Tom Williams|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/labour-scraps-plans-create-new-uk-academy-mathematics}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2024/09/26/labour-ditches-rishi-sunak-national-maths-academy-plan/|date=2024-09-26|author=Sarah Knapton|publisher=[[Daily Telegraph]]|title=Labour ‘disappoints’ academics by ditching Sunak’s national maths academy}}</ref>

==Organisation==
The academy is registered as a [[charitable incorporated organisation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://register-of-charities.charitycommission.gov.uk/en/charity-search/-/charity-details/5220516|title=ACADEMY FOR THE MATHEMATICAL SCIENCES|publisher=[[Charity Commission]]}}</ref> It is hosted by the [[Isaac Newton Institute]] (INI) in Cambridge, UK. After an open application process, Alison Etheridge was announced as the first president in May 2024.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.researchprofessionalnews.com/rr-news-uk-charities-and-societies-2024-5-president-revealed-for-new-uk-maths-academy|publisher=Research Professional News|title=President revealed for UK maths academy contender|date=2024-05-13|author=Rachel Magee}}</ref> The chair of trustees and vice president is Nigel Campbell, a former civil servant and government analyst; the executive director is Dr [[Christie Marr]], previously deputy director at INI.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acadmathsci.org.uk/governance/team/|title=Trustees, Fellows, Executive Committee, & Advisory Board|publisher=Academy for the Mathematical Sciences}}</ref>

The academy works across the UK and the nations of Wales,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.learnedsociety.wales/lsw-events/what-the-academy-for-the-mathematical-sciences-can-do-for-us/|title=What the (Academy for the) Mathematical Sciences can do for us|publisher=[[Learned Society of Wales]]|year=2025}}</ref> Northern Ireland<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ria.ie/2025/04/22/belfast-meeting-of-uk-academy-for-the-mathematical-sciences/|title=Belfast meeting of UK Academy for the Mathematical Sciences|publisher=[[Royal Irish Academy]]|year=2025}}</ref> and Scotland.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://icms.ac.uk/the-academy-for-the-mathematical-sciences-maths-manifesto-for-scotland/|title=The Academy for the Mathematical Sciences Maths Manifesto for Scotland|publisher=[[International Centre for Mathematical Sciences]]|year=2025}}</ref> The [[Council for the Mathematical Sciences]] has been subsumed into the new academy, as its Learned Societies Forum.<ref>{{cite magazine|periodical=Dianoia|volume=13|issue=3|url=https://iciam.org/news/25/7/7/strengthening-mathematical-collaboration-uk-council-mathematical-sciences-becomes|title=Strengthening Mathematical Collaboration in the UK: The Council for Mathematical Sciences Becomes the Learned Societies Forum|publisher=[[International_Council_for_Industrial_and_Applied_Mathematics|ICIAM]]|year=2025}}</ref> The academy has also formed an education committee, chaired by [[Lynne McClure]],<ref>{{cite letter|title=Government response to Maths education letter|url=https://committees.parliament.uk/publications/48483/documents/253963/default/|author=[[Catherine McKinnell]] MP|date=2025-06-13|recipient=[[Lord Mair]]}}</ref> to represent the interests of maths education in the UK.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hansard.parliament.uk/Lords/2024-10-31/debates/C172BA44-A670-4DDF-B253-6859A418109B/ScienceAndTechnologyEconomy|title=Science and Technology: Economy|volume=840|at=col1304|publisher=House of Lords}}</ref>

==Fellowship==
The 100 founding fellows of the academy were announced on 29 January 2026<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acadmathsci.org.uk/2026/01/29/acadmathsci-appoints-its-founding-fellows/|title=AcadMathSci appoints its first cohort of fellows|publisher=Academy for the Mathematical Sciences|year=2026}}</ref> after an open competition.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]|url=https://imstat.org/2025/07/16/acadmathsci-seeks-fellows/|title=AcadMathSci seeks Fellows|date=2025-07-16}}</ref> They comprise leading mathematical researchers and practitioners in education,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ayrshire-today.co.uk/news/25828357.teacher-kilmarnocks-grange-academy-given-huge-honour/|publisher=Ayrshire Today|date=2026-02-05|title=Teacher at Kilmarnock's Grange Academy given huge honour|author=Claire Lindsay}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|publisher=Derry Now|url=https://www.derrynow.com/news/local-news/2001077/derry-mathematician-inaugurated-into-academy-for-the-mathematical-sciences.html|title=Derry mathematician inaugurated into Academy for the Mathematical Sciences|date=2026-01-29|author=Catherine McGinty}}</ref> academia, industry and government.  The science minister [[Patrick Vallance]] was quoted: <blockquote>The Academy for the Mathematical Sciences’ inaugural Fellows represent the very best of this national capability, and I commend the Academy for bringing them together. Their expertise strengthens our security, boosts productivity and supports high‑quality jobs across the country, so it is only right that they are celebrated.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2026-01-29-oxford-academics-among-first-fellows-academy-mathematical-sciences|publisher=University of Oxford|title=Oxford academics among the first Fellows of the Academy for the Mathematical Sciences|year=2026}}</ref></blockquote>

Notable fellows include [[John Aston (statistician)|John Aston]], [[June Barrow-Green]], [[Veronica Bowman]], [[Margaret Brown (mathematics educator)|Margaret Brown]], [[Christopher Budd (mathematician)|Chris Budd]], [[Kevin Buzzard]], [[Ana Caraiani]], [[José A. Carrillo|Jose Antonio Carrillo de la Plata]], [[Gui-Qiang Chen|Gui Qiang George Chen]], [[Rama Cont]], [[Anne-Christine Davis]], [[Claudia de Rham]], [[Simon Donaldson]], [[Christl Donnelly]], [[Paul Glaister]], [[Paul Glendinning]], [[Leslie Ann Goldberg]], [[Darryl Holm]], [[Kevin Houston (mathematician)|Kevin Houston]], [[Celia Hoyles]], [[Daniel J. Hulme|Daniel Hulme]], [[Eugénie Hunsicker]], [[Anne Keast-Butler]], [[Minhyong Kim]], [[Ruth King (statistician)|Ruth King]], [[James Maynard (mathematician)|James Maynard]], [[Guy Nason]], [[Simon Peyton-Jones]], [[Lasse Rempe]], [[Richard Samworth]], [[Carola-Bibiane Schönlieb]], [[Jennifer Scott (mathematician)|Jennifer Scott]], [[Bobby Seagull]], [[David Silver (computer scientist)|David Silver]], [[David Spiegelhalter]], [[Gwyneth Stallard]], [[Aris Syntetos]], [[Jack Thorne (mathematician)|Jack Thorne]], [[Sarah L. Waters|Sarah Waters]], [[Wendelin Werner]] and [[Helen Wilson (mathematician)|Helen Wilson]].
